teaser: A book told by its cast: the nine agents of The Ultimate Insider became characters with moods, fears and running jokes, every trait from the record.
core_idea: From a page-7 panel of the talk's nine agents, the editor asked for characters and then for the book to be told by them, with moods, interviews, therapy and himself as narrator; within twelve hours the team drew nine characters by code with four moods and a scorecard each, and wrote a character bible in which every trait rests on the record, scenes are dramatised and say so, claims about how agents work are checked, and failures stay in; the idea runs back through the Gen ZX storyboards and the editor's pen notes, carried across by a review, and the team held two minutes after writing a scene about a hold.

Every trait rests on the record.
Was the brake late? Or was it right on time? You can tell me.
